HOW: Keep the Thread reference, join it with a timeout after deletedAll.set(true) before asserting.

WHAT: Reader thread busy-spins full listings with maxResults=Integer.MAX_VALUE and no throttle. WHY: Each iteration loads all groups with no pagination/backoff, creating unbounded request fanout and server load that can starve the deleter and destabilize the suite. HOW: Bound the page size and add backoff/yield between iterations.

Race: the reader Thread is not retained/joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. deletedAll.set(true) does not wait for an in-flight groups() call, so an exception arriving after the assert is missed (false pass) and the thread can leak into the next test. Join the reader thread (with timeout) after setting deletedAll and before the assertion.

The reader thread is started but never joined before assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()). deletedAll.set(true) does not wait for an in-flight groups() call, so exceptions added after the assert are missed and the test can falsely pass. Keep the Thread reference and join it (with timeout) after setting deletedAll and before asserting.

The reader thread is not joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty: deletedAll is set then assertion runs while a groups() call may still be in flight, so an exception caused by the concurrent-delete bug would be added after the check and the test would still pass. Keep a Thread reference and join() it before asserting.

Background reader Thread is started but never joined before assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()). deletedAll only stops the next loop iteration; a read already in flight can add an exception after the assert, so the test can spuriously pass. Keep the Thread handle and join (with timeout) after deletedAll.set(true) before asserting.

issues.descricao: The cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, violating the GroupModel contract that it never returns null and risking NPEs in callers that unbox it.
issues.textoGolden: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). Returning null here breaks that convention and can surface as an unboxing/NPE on the consumer side of the read path. Return a non-null value (e.g., 0) or only null if the GroupModel contract explicitly declares it nullable.

issues.descricao: The concurrency regression test never waits for the reader thread before asserting no exceptions, so it can pass even when the concurrent-deletion NPE still occurs.
issues.textoGolden: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

comentarios.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.

The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.

issues.descricao: The reader thread's stop flag is set only after all deletions succeed, so a failing delete leaves a non-daemon thread polling indefinitely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: prefix/suffix trimming computes start and end independently with no overlap guard, so value.substring(start, value.length() - end) throws when start + end exceeds length. WHY: aborts the whole theme verification with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the offending key. HOW: cap the suffix scan by the remaining length (end < length - start) before substring.

WHAT: verifySafeHtml throws unchecked RuntimeException when the translation or derived English file cannot be read. WHY: an absent English counterpart (new locale file or bad resources-community mapping) crashes the Maven build with a stack trace instead of a collectable verification error. HOW: throw MojoExecutionException or record the failure in messages like other checks.

The Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 value is now Italian ('Installa una delle...'), so Lithuanian users will see Italian. Restore a Lithuanian translation (without vendor links, matching the other locales' intent) instead of the Italian copy-paste.
The Lithuanian totpStep1 value is now Italian, same copy-paste error as the login bundle. Lithuanian account users will see Italian. Provide the Lithuanian translation instead.

The zh_CN value uses Traditional forms (手機, 應用程式, 安裝) instead of Simplified (手机, 应用程序, 安装). Simplified-Chinese users get the wrong script variant. Use the Simplified wording consistent with the rest of the zh_CN file.

The suffix-strip loop allows end to grow past start when one string is a prefix-extension of the other (e.g. value='aaa' vs sanitized='aa': start=2, end=2), making value.substring(start, value.length()-end) throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Bound the suffix scan by the remaining length (end < length - start).

Prefix/suffix trimming computes start and end independently; when they overlap (one string is prefix of the other) value.substring(start,value.length-end) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and aborts verification instead of reporting Illegal HTML. Clamp end to length-start before substring.
File declares locale lt but new totpStep1 value is Italian, not Lithuanian. Readers of the lt theme will see the wrong language. Replace with Lithuanian text without HTML anchors.
File declares locale lt but new loginTotpStep1 value is Italian, not Lithuanian. Same wrong-language substitution as the account bundle. Replace with Lithuanian text without HTML anchors.
File declares zh_CN (Simplified) but new value uses Traditional forms手機/應用程式. Use Simplified手机/应用程序 to match the declared locale.

issues.descricao: The Lithuanian TOTP setup step was replaced with Italian text in both the account and login bundles.
issues.textoGolden: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).

comentarios.texto: The Lithuanian OTP setup instruction has been replaced with an Italian sentence. login-config-totp.ftl renders this message directly, so users selecting Lithuanian receive an instruction in the wrong language; the same copied sentence also appears in the Lithuanian account bundle at line 101. Replace both values with the Lithuanian translation of the new installation instruction.

The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian (“Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare”), but this is the Lithuanian locale and the surrounding setup steps are Lithuanian. Translate the new instruction into Lithuanian rather than copying the Italian translation. The same incorrect replacement appears in the login bundle at themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71 and should be corrected there too; otherwise Lithuanian users see an untranslated first step in both OTP setup flows.

The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian, not Lithuanian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`). The same replacement was made for `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle. Translate both replacements into Lithuanian so selecting Lithuanian does not display Italian instructions during authenticator setup.

issues.textoGolden: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.

comentarios.texto: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) file was given Traditional Chinese characters: totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：. Compare the unchanged neighbouring lines (e.g. '打开应用扫描二维码…') which use Simplified forms; 手機/應用程式/安裝 are Traditional. zh_CN must be Simplified Chinese, so this string is in the wrong script/variant for the locale.

issues.descricao: The method santizeAnchors is misspelled; it should be sanitizeAnchors.
issues.textoGolden: The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').

issues.descricao: HTML_TAGS is a non-static, non-private field instead of a private static final constant.
issues.textoGolden: Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

issues.descricao: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

comentarios.texto: The common prefix (start) and common suffix (end) are computed independently and can overlap, for example value "aa" vs sanitized "a". Then substring(start, length - end) gets begin > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan so that start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length()), e.g. `while (end < min - start && ...)`.

The common prefix and common suffix are computed independently and can overlap, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` can have start > end and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This crashes the verifier instead of reporting 'Illegal HTML'. Cap the suffix scan with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

WHAT: Common prefix/suffix stripping for the diff message can compute start+end larger than the string length and call substring(start, length-end) with start > end. WHY: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the key loop and crashes verification instead of reporting Illegal HTML. HOW: Clamp end so start+end <= min lengths, e.g. stop suffix scan when end >= length-start.

issues.descricao: normalizeValue blanks the entire choice expression for some keys before HTML validation, so markup placed inside a choice branch of those keys bypasses the new verifier.

comentarios.texto: Choice normalization removes all branch content before HTML validation, allowing prohibited markup to bypass the new translation policy. A translated error-invalid-multivalued-size value such as `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1

WHAT: normalizeValue replaces the entire {n,choice,...} block with ... before sanitizing, so HTML inside choice options is never checked. WHY: A translation can smuggle tags (e.g. {2,choice,0#<script>...}) in error-invalid-multivalued-size/linkExpirationFormatter keys and pass the verifier, reaching UI rendering as XSS. HOW: Sanitize/validate the choice body instead of blanking it, or run the HTML policy on the inner choice text as well.

issues.descricao: The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

comentarios.texto: The admin-ui bundle is consumed by react-i18next, which interpolates with double-brace `{{0}}` syntax (the previous value was `Attribute {{0}} ... {{2}}`). This line was rewritten to Java MessageFormat/ICU syntax (`{0}` ... `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), which i18next does not understand: the placeholders will not be substituted and the literal `{2,choice,...}` text will be shown to users. Keep the JS-side value in `{{0}}` form (and don't introduce ICU ChoiceFormat into the JS bundle); the ICU/choice spelling belongs only in the Java theme properties.

Same contract break in the account-ui bundle: the value was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` (i18next double-brace interpolation) and was changed to `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` MessageFormat+ICU syntax. The account console's i18next based consumer was not updated to match, so interpolation will fail and the raw placeholder/choice syntax will be rendered. Restore `{{0}}`-style placeholders for the JS bundle.

The account-ui bundle is consumed by i18next, which interpolates with double braces (the original string was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`). This PR aligned the value to the Java theme convention, replacing `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` with `{0}/{1}/{2}` and adding ICU `{2,choice,...}`. i18next will no longer substitute the placeholders and cannot interpret the ICU choice, so the account UI shows the raw `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and literal choice text. Keep the JS-side double-brace form for this bundle (adapt the choice accordingly) rather than the Java single-brace/ICU form used by the theme messages.

issues.descricao: If the English counterpart of a messages_*.properties file does not exist, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException that escapes the mojo, crashing the build instead of reporting a validation message.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The event listener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled() which in ClientPermissionsV2 unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. WHY: Deleting a client/role/group while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is active crashes the removal flow instead of cleaning up. HOW: Skip V1 cleanup when V2 is enabled (V2 has no per-object permissions) or guard with !isFeatureEnabled(V2).

WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) dereferences the all-clients type resource without null-check before findByResource. WHY: On a fresh realm with no Clients type resource, getResourceTypeResource returns null and the policy-store lookup throws NPE, breaking every canManage/canView/canConfigure check.

WHAT: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles only check fine-grained permission and never check MANAGE_CLIENTS role, unlike canManage/canManageClientScopes siblings. WHY: A realm admin with manage-clients (or existing V1 behavior) is incorrectly denied role-mapping on clients, breaking the implied-admin contract.

WHAT: getClientsWithPermission calls root.evaluatePermission separately for every Clients-type resource inside findByType. WHY: Listing/filtering clients triggers O(N) full policy evaluations with N growing with client count, causing material slowdown on large realms.

setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but AdminPermissions still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled on ClientRemovedEvent. When clients() is V2 via MgmtPermissionsV2, any client deletion throws out of the event listener, aborting the transaction. Make it a no-op in V2 (no per-client state) or guard the listener for V2.

Javadoc says Returns true but method is void requireView() that throws ForbiddenException. Copy-paste from canView above; contradicts signature and neighbouring require* docs. Fix to Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false.

Javadoc says Returns true but method is void requireViewClientScopes() that throws ForbiddenException. Contradicts signature and neighbouring require* docs. Fix to Throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false.

ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled now always throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions ProviderEventListener still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled on ClientRemovedEvent when fine-grained authz is enabled. In V2 that call will throw (breaking client deletion/event handling) instead of being a no-op. Guard the listener for V2 or make the V2 override a no-op.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on a fresh context.form() instance that is then discarded before rendering. WHY: callers (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler before challenge(), WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse before fillContextForm()+errorChallenge) each obtain new LoginFormsProvider instances to render, so the re-auth error page loses hidden-username state and falls back to regular login form. HOW: thread the same LoginFormsProvider instance through — set the attributes on the form used by challenge/fill/errorChallenge instead of calling context.form() inside the helper.

issues.descricao: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

comentarios.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: The comment 'setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' does not mention that the condition also requires a selected user to own a passkey credential.

comentarios.texto: The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

issues.descricao: The test comment says it sets the passwordless policy for discoverable keys, but the updater only disables passkeys for the realm.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.

issues.descricao: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the realm, so the hidden webauthn form is guaranteed by isPasskeysEnabled() and the new per-user isConfiguredFor check for users without a passkey is never exercised in UsernamePasswordForm.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getLoginPredicate dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check on the new BROKER_PUBLIC clause. WHY: any IdentityProviderModel with a null config map (e.g. newly constructed model before persistence) throws NPE when create/update/remove call registerIDPLoginInvalidation, breaking the write path.

WHAT: getForLogin stores one IdentityProviderListQuery per FetchMode containing a searchKey entry per distinct organizationId queried. WHY: with many organizations each distinct login query appends a new map entry to the same revisioned cache object, causing unbounded memory growth and larger replication payloads per realm.

Cache-hit path in getForLogin() returns raw getById() models while the miss/invalid path maps through createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. Resolve then wrap each cached IDP before adding, so both paths return the same enriched type.

Fixture makes new predicate `orgId==null || BROKER_PUBLIC` vacuously true: realm IdPs satisfy first disjunct, all 10 org-linked IdPs set BROKER_PUBLIC=true. Add at least one org-linked non-public (private) IdP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts; otherwise deleting/inverting that clause leaves counts 5/5/10 unchanged and the test still passes.

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.
remove() always queries idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias), adding a database lookup on every IDP removal even when the cached entry already holds the model.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with events.values() via zip, but get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id whose values() order need not match error_ids order. WHY: mismatched id/data pairs attach wrong title/message/timestamp to errors and corrupt chronological interleaving in get_request_data. HOW: look up each id by its node_id instead of zipping values().

WHAT: validate_timestamp/validate_age test mutual exclusion with truthiness (initial_data.get(...)) so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypasses the check. WHY: reports containing both fields with a zero value incorrectly pass validation, breaking the Working-Draft vs Editor-Draft exclusivity contract. HOW: test key presence ("age" in initial_data) instead of truthiness.

WHAT: update() reads validated_data.get("detector_type") but the serializer field is `type` (validated by validate_type) and create() uses validated_data["type"]. WHY: the lookup always misses and falls back to instance.group_type, so detector type changes via PUT are silently ignored. HOW: read validated_data.get("type", instance.group_type).

WHAT: the use-table-widget-visualization branch renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns/data/meta instead of result.data, result.meta, fields and eventView. WHY: enabling the flag blanks every dashboard table widget, a user-visible data-loss regression. HOW: omit if speculative beyond wiring real result through.

WHAT: column fallback reads tableData?.meta.fields but only guards tableData, so meta===undefined throws TypeError while data uses tableData?.data ?? []. WHY: any empty/partial TabularData (e.g. the empty placeholder above) crashes render instead of showing an empty table. HOW: guard meta with tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}.

WHAT: analytics.record fires before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check. WHY: disabled-flag and rejected requests pollute analytics and record user/project IDs for requests that should be no-ops. HOW: move the record call after the feature gate.

WHAT: tag.key (which can be tags[...,number] or contain slashes/spaces) is interpolated directly into the request path. WHY: keys with / break routing to a wrong endpoint and brackets/commas produce malformed URLs, letting crafted attribute names alter the request target. HOW: encode with encodeURIComponent(attributeKey).

WHAT: the endpoint loops over an attacker-controlled unauthenticated raw_data list with no size cap, validating each item and emitting metrics. WHY: a single request with a huge array burns CPU on DRF validation and fans out unbounded metrics.incr calls, enabling cheap request-amplification DoS. HOW: enforce a max batch size before the loop.

get_multi returns dict keyed by node_id; zipping error_ids with events.values() assumes order and equal length. Missing keys shift pairs, attributing wrong title/message to wrong id. Look up each node_id via dict get instead.

validate_timestamp uses `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age uses `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Falsy-but-present values (age=0, timestamp=0) are treated as absent, so mutually-exclusive check is bypassed. Use explicit existence check (`"age" in self.initial_data` / `is not None`) instead of truthiness.

`events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict with no order guarantee; `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes values() order equals error_ids order and stays aligned when an entry is missing (None values are filtered after zipping, shifting alignment). Look up per-id via node_id instead of zipping values().

issues.descricao: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
issues.textoGolden: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

comentarios.texto: The timestamp/age validators test truthiness and make both fields optional instead of enforcing exactly one field. Reports with both age=0 and timestamp=0, or with neither field, pass validation despite violating the stated mutually exclusive report formats. Enforce field presence and exclusivity in object-level validate using key membership rather than truthiness.

Check key presence rather than truthiness when enforcing age/timestamp mutual exclusion. Both fields permit 0, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 passes both validators even though both fields are present; a zero-valued counterpart also bypasses the corresponding check. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or object-level validation) and add zero-value tests.

Check field presence rather than truthiness when enforcing timestamp/age exclusivity. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes both validators, despite the declared constraint that they must not coexist; with only one zero value, validation is also asymmetric. Use membership checks on initial_data (or object-level validation) and add zero-value mixed-field tests.

issues.descricao: The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.

comentarios.texto: The new validation-failure warning logs `raw_report`, the full unvalidated report object supplied by the caller. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated (permission_classes = (), @csrf_exempt), so the payload is attacker-controlled, and browser report bodies routinely carry sensitive values (CSP blocked-uri/document-uri/script-sample, sourceFile, plus the full user_agent). Logging the raw payload on every validation failure writes potentially sensitive data into application logs; log only the report `type` (or a sanitized/redacted subset) instead of the entire raw object.

Do not attach the complete raw report to the validation warning. Browser reports contain page URLs (potentially including tokens or personal data in query strings) and arbitrary body contents. Any invalid field now causes that entire payload to be emitted at warning level, exposing it in operational logs even where the existing info-level request logging is filtered out. Log the failed field names/report type or a redacted diagnostic instead.

issues.descricao: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids positionally with nodestore get_multi values, but get_multi does not preserve input order (cached items are appended last) and drops missing nodes, so error details get attached to the wrong error IDs.
issues.textoGolden: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() instead of mapping by node_id, misaligning ids to payloads and dropping/mismatching on missing keys. WHY: assigns wrong title/message/timestamp to wrong error id and yields incorrect Seer logs. HOW: look up each node_id in the get_multi dict (e.g. dict keyed by node_id) and preserve error_ids order.

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` values preserve input order and that all keys exist. Dict values give no such guarantee; missing keys shorten/misalign the zip, attaching the wrong event payload to the wrong error_id. Lookup per-id: iterate node_ids/error_ids and do `events.get(node_id)` instead of zipping with `.values()`.

fetch_error_details pairs IDs to payloads with zip(error_ids, events.values()) where events is dict from nodestore get_multi. Values order need not match IDs and missing keys misalign, attaching wrong title/message to wrong error. Look up per node_id instead.

issues.descricao: The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

comentarios.texto: The new Snuba replay lookup executes even when enable_error_context=false. Every opt-out summary request incurs an unnecessary database round trip and can now fail on Snuba availability even though it only needs recording storage. Evaluate the flag first and perform the replay lookup only when error context is enabled.

issues.descricao: With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `use-table-widget-visualization` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, hardcoding empty rows and no columns instead of the actual query result. WHY: when the feature flag is enabled for an org, every table widget renders an empty table and silently drops `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns`, a functional regression for all dashboard table widgets. HOW: build `columns`/`tableData` from the existing `result` (and `widget.queries[i].fields`/`fieldAliases`) rather than the empty placeholder objects.

In the new feature-flagged branch, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty props: columns={[]} (an empty array, which is truthy for the `columns ?? fallback` logic, so no columns are derived) and tableData={data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}. All the real result data computed above (result.data, result.meta, fields, fieldAliases, eventView) is discarded, so any organization with 'use-table-widget-visualization' enabled gets an empty table instead of the query results. Pass the actual result data/columns into the visualization (or keep the old StyledSimpleTableChart) until the widget is properly wired.

With the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty data/meta instead of result.data and result.meta. Every table widget therefore renders empty for orgs with the flag. Fix: pass tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}} and build columns from the fields.

issues.descricao: The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.

comentarios.texto: The documented custom-renderer contract says fallback runs when the callback returns undefined, but `if (cell)` also falls back for valid ReactNode results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null`. A caller trying to render zero or deliberately suppress a cell instead gets the default field rendering. Check `cell !== undefined` here and in the head-cell renderer so the implementation honors the advertised contract.

Use `cell !== undefined` instead of `if (cell)` to select the custom renderer result, and apply the same correction to the header renderer. The API documents undefined as the fallback sentinel, but valid ReactNode results such as numeric 0, an empty string, or null are falsy. A custom renderer returning 0 or intentionally hiding a cell with null therefore unexpectedly renders the default value instead.

issues.descricao: The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

comentarios.texto: The new attribute query key omits the organization even though its query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Switching organizations with identical project selections such as all projects and the same date range reuses the singleton query client's prior organization's attribute metadata, including while the new request refetches. Include organization.slug or organization.id in the query key.

Include the organization slug in this query key. The new useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys implementation fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions contains no organization identity. Two organizations with identical filters (particularly the default all-project selection) therefore share this cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attribute names, and concurrently mounted consumers can reuse a request for the wrong organization. Preserve the organization-specific cache identity that the previous endpoint-based key provided.

Include the organization slug or ID in this query key. The query function fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but the key contains only query options. Two organizations with the same project selection (especially the all-projects selection), date range and dataset therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attributes, and overlapping requests can populate the shared entry with the wrong organization's result.

issues.descricao: The UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps doc says only LOGS is supported, although the hooks are also used with SPANS.

comentarios.texto: The new shared prop documentation claims the endpoint currently supports only LOGS, but this PR also uses these hooks with TraceItemDataset.SPANS (for example in TransactionNameSearchBar). Update this comment to describe both supported datasets; as written it incorrectly tells callers that a supported and actively used input is unsupported.

issues.descricao: Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.
dedupedYAxes is now just [yAxis], so its name misdescribes the code.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
BrowserReportSerializer's validate_timestamp/validate_age docstrings claim one of age/timestamp must be present, but the code only enforces mutual exclusion, so reports with neither are accepted.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for processes created via mp_context.Process (SpawnProcess is a sibling of multiprocessing.Process, both subclass BaseProcess). WHY: kill() in _ensure_processes_alive and terminate() in join() are therefore never executed for real flusher processes, leaving hung/crashed processes alive while a replacement is started (duplicate flushing, fd/Kafka-producer leak, zombie on shutdown). HOW: drop the isinstance gate and duck-type (try kill/terminate, ignore ValueError/AttributeError for threading.Thread) or check multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess.

WHAT: Negative max_processes passes the `or` fallback and min() yields a negative num_processes, so range() is empty and no flusher process is ever created. WHY: Consumer keeps committing offsets while nothing ever flushes Redis, causing unbounded Redis growth and silent segment loss. HOW: Clamp/validate to >=1 and raise on invalid values.

WHAT: get_memory_info() returns cluster-wide iter_cluster_memory_usage via the same Redis client for every shard_buffer, but submit() calls it once per flusher process and sums the duplicated results. WHY: Performs N redundant Redis INFO scans per message (plus N record_stored_segments pipelines at lines 269-270), scaling linearly with flusher_processes on every submit. HOW: Query memory info once from a single buffer/client.

WHAT: time.sleep is monkeypatched to `lambda _: None` at test start, so the added time.sleep(0.1) does nothing. WHY: Flusher thread may not observe current_drift before join() sets stopped, making the single-message assertion flaky/races. HOW: Use the real clock for the wait or poll until messages appear with a deadline.

Docstring is made untrue by the sharding pool added in this PR: num_processes can be less than shard count via max_processes/flusher_processes, with multiple shards per process. Update docstring to describe distribution rather than one-process-per-shard.

wait_produce timer uses tag key shards while produce timer and segment_size in the same function use shard. The keys must agree or dashboards/alerts filtering by one key will miss the other series. Change shards to shard.

time.sleep is patched to a no-op at test start, so the added time.sleep(0.1) meant to let flusher threads process returns immediately. The assertion after races with background threads and would pass/fail independent of flush completion.

test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal counts (num processes and mapped shard total) and joins without producing anything. If shard sharing/mapping were broken (wrong shards per process, dropped data, no flush when processes < shards) the test would still pass.

Processes are created via get_context('spawn').Process but restart checks isinstance against default multiprocessing.Process, which fails for SpawnProcess so hung flusher is never killed before replacement.
Same mismatch in join(): spawn processes fail isinstance check so terminate() is skipped, leaking workers on shutdown.

issues.descricao: The wait_produce timer is tagged with 'shards' while sibling flusher metrics use 'shard' for the same value, so per-shard dashboards miss it.
issues.textoGolden: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

comentarios.texto: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with the key `"shards"`, while the other two metrics emitted in this same loop (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce` at line 185 and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` at line 195) use the key `"shard"`. All three carry the same `shard_tag` value, so this is a pure key-name disagreement: any dashboard or alert that groups/filters by the `shard` tag will silently receive no data from `wait_produce`. Rename the tag key to `"shard"` so all flusher metrics share one tag.

The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with key `shards` while every sibling metric introduced/updated in the same method (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`) uses the singular key `shard`. Anything consuming this metric family by the `shard` tag (dashboards, alerts, tag-based aggregation) will silently receive no data for `wait_produce`, and per-shard breakdowns of produce latency will be incomplete. Change the tag to `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` so the tag contract matches the other flusher metrics.

The wait_produce timer tags with "shards", while the sibling metrics in the same loop use "shard" for the same value (shard_tag). Use one tag key, "shard", so queries and dashboards that group by it cover all of these metrics.

issues.descricao: The time.sleep(0.1) added to test_basic to let flusher threads process is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep.
issues.textoGolden: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The added synchronization point `time.sleep(0.1)` added after the second `step.poll()` is neutralized by the test's own `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 15 (same `time` module), so it does not actually wait. WHY: The comment says it 'Give[s] flusher threads time to process after drift change', but the call is a no-op, so the test still races the background flusher thread before `step.join()` and is liable to be flaky / to not exercise the intended post-drift flush path. HOW: Use a non-monkeypatched wait (e.g. capture the real sleep before patching, or use the flusher's thread/process join, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a real timeout).

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait: line 15 of the same test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces `sleep` on the global `time` module, so this call (and the flusher's own `time.sleep`) is a no-op. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is therefore false — the call returns instantly and provides no synchronisation, so the test does not actually wait for the flusher to process after the drift change. Either synchronise on a real condition (e.g. wait until the expected message is produced) or, if the original `time.sleep` is needed here, patch a module-scoped reference instead of the global `time.sleep`.

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so nothing waits for the flusher threads before `step.join()` and the `messages` assertion. Replace it with a condition-based wait, such as polling until `messages` is non-empty with a deadline. Use the real sleep saved before patching if a delay is needed.

issues.descricao: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
issues.textoGolden: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

comentarios.texto: The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard does not match the SpawnProcess instances created by self.mp_context.Process. When a worker hangs, the guard skips kill() and the replacement starts while the original worker remains alive, allowing overlapping flushing of the same shards if the original resumes and leaking hung workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or self.mp_context.Process, and kill and join the old worker before replacing it.

The workers are created with get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances; these are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class). Consequently this guard skips kill() for actual production workers. When a worker hangs, the replacement starts while the original remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the spawn-context Process class for the check, and fix the identical check in join() so shutdown also terminates surviving workers.

Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the separate multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this guard skips kill() for production workers. When a live worker exceeds max-unhealthy-seconds, the code starts a replacement and overwrites its handle while the original is still running. If the original resumes, both workers flush the same shards, and repeated hangs can exceed the configured process limit. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or explicitly distinguish threads) and stop the old worker before replacing it.

issues.descricao: join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.
issues.textoGolden: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

comentarios.texto: join() breaks out of the worker loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping cleanup for every remaining worker. If next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier worker exhausts it, remaining flushers can continue running after shutdown or partition reassignment. Use the deadline only to limit waiting and still terminate and reap every remaining process.

Do not break out of worker cleanup when the join deadline expires. If the first worker consumes the timeout, the next iteration breaks before terminating that worker or any subsequent workers. They may still be blocked in Redis or producer calls despite the shared stopped flag, leaving old workers running after strategy shutdown/reassignment. Apply the deadline only to waiting, and perform termination cleanup for every worker regardless of remaining time (using a type check that recognizes spawn-context workers).
join() waits for processes sequentially against a single shared deadline and breaks without terminating remaining processes once it expires, leaking them.

issues.descricao: The SpanFlusher docstring says it creates one process per shard, but shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

comentarios.texto: The docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the code at lines 60-66 shares shards across a capped number of processes (num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)); each shard assigned via i % self.num_processes). With the new --flusher-processes default of 1, a single process handles every shard, so the documented contract is the opposite of the behaviour this PR introduces (confirmed by test_flusher_processes_limit, which asserts 4 shards served by 2 processes). Update the docstring to say shards are distributed across up to max_processes flusher processes.

The new docstring says this creates one process per shard, but workers are capped by max_processes and shards are distributed among them. In particular, the CLI default of 1 means all assigned shards share one process. Describe capped workers with potentially multiple shards per worker so callers do not rely on per-shard process isolation.

The docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard', but the number of processes is capped by max_processes (--flusher-processes), and shards are shared across processes via i % num_processes. Reword it to say that shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

issues.descricao: max_processes uses a truthiness fallback, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes one process per shard instead of being rejected.

comentarios.texto: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats a falsy value as 'not provided'. The new `--flusher-processes` click option is `type=int`, so a user can pass `0`; that legitimate-but-falsy value is discarded and the flusher silently spawns one process per shard instead of honoring the requested limit. Use an explicit None check, e.g. `self.max_processes = max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (and validate/reject 0 upstream).

An explicit max_processes=0 is treated as an omitted limit by `or`, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` starts one process per assigned shard instead of respecting or rejecting the supplied zero limit. The CLI accepts zero as an integer and the factory forwards it unchanged. Default only when max_processes is None, and explicitly validate that supplied process limits are positive so zero cannot silently enable potentially many workers.

`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses a truthiness test, so an explicit 0 is treated as 'unset' and silently expands to one process per shard. Use `max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and reject values below 1.

issues.descricao: A negative --flusher-processes value is not validated and makes SpanFlusher construction fail with KeyError.

comentarios.texto: `flusher_processes` is not validated to be >= 1. `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` lets a negative value through (it is truthy), so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative and `range(self.num_processes)` is empty, leaving `process_to_shards_map` as `{}`. The following loop computes `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, which for any negative divisor is 0, so `self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard)` raises KeyError and the consumer fails to construct. Since `flusher_processes` is exposed as an int CLI option (`--flusher-processes`), a negative value is reachable from configuration. Guard with `max(1, self.num_processes)` / validate the input.
negative max_processes flows through `or` guard into min() -> empty map -> KeyError on i % num_processes; empty assigned_shards yields zero processes.

issues.descricao: submit() queries cluster-wide Redis memory once per flusher buffer, repeating identical INFO calls per process on every submit.

comentarios.texto: The new loop calls get_memory_info() once per flusher buffer even though SpansBuffer.get_memory_info delegates to iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client), which fetches INFO for the entire Redis cluster regardless of assigned_shards. With P flusher processes and memory backpressure enabled, each submitted batch now performs P identical cluster-wide memory queries on the consumer thread instead of one, increasing Redis traffic and blocking ingestion. Fetch cluster memory information once from a single buffer.
submit() loop calls buffer.get_memory_info() per flusher but each call is cluster-wide from same client, repeating identical INFO N× per submit.

issues.descricao: _create_process_for_shard is added but never called.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is newly added but has no caller anywhere (grep for `_create_process_for_shard(` finds only its definition); the restart path actually used is `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. WHY: This is dead code that indicates the intended per-shard restart wiring was left incomplete — any future caller relying on restarting only the process owning a given shard will silently do nothing, and it is confusing which restart path is authoritative. HOW: Remove `_create_process_for_shard`, or wire it into `_ensure_processes_alive` if per-shard restart was intended.

issues.descricao: test_flusher_processes_limit counts assigned shards instead of checking that each shard is assigned exactly once.

comentarios.texto: The assertion counts shard entries rather than verifying shard assignment. A broken distribution such as {0: [0, 1], 1: [0, 1]} still passes all assertions in this test while shards 2 and 3 are never flushed. Assert that the flattened mapping contains exactly the expected assigned shards, with no duplicates (and verify each worker's shard buffer uses that mapping), rather than only asserting a total of four.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import so every AssignmentSource shares the same timestamp. WHY: breaks any recency/ordering use of `queued` and makes to_dict/from_dict round-trips carry a stale time. HOW: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

WHAT: `to_dict()` via `asdict` keeps `queued` as a raw datetime, which is passed as celery `apply_async` kwargs in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. WHY: the datetime is not JSON-serializable so outbound assignee sync tasks fail to serialize/enqueue instead of syncing. HOW: serialize `queued` to isoformat string in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

WHAT: `from_dict` passes a serialized `queued` string straight into a datetime field with no coercion, and returns None on any unexpected/missing key. WHY: a None source makes `should_sync(..., None)` return True, silently disabling the cycle guard the PR adds and resuming the loop. HOW: coerce/validate `queued`, `source_name`, and `integration_id` explicitly as above.

WHAT: base `sync_status_outbound` adds explicit `assignment_source` param but `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` accepts no **kwargs. WHY: any caller passing `assignment_source=` to that installation raises TypeError, breaking the override contract. HOW: keep the new param absorbed via **kwargs on the base or update all overrides to accept it.

to_dict() returns raw datetime in queued via asdict, passed as assignment_source_dict to apply_async kwargs. Celery JSON encoder has no rule for datetime so enqueue raises. Serialize to ISO string and parse back in from_dict, use default_factory for queued.

The default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class definition, so all AssignmentSource instances share the import-time timestamp instead of creation time. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so `queued` reflects actual creation/queue time.

to_dict() leaves queued as datetime but it is sent through Celery apply_async kwargs which must be JSON-serializable and read back by from_dict() with no ISO-string parsing. Serialize queued to isoformat (and parse back in from_dict) so outbound assignee sync does not fail serialization or round-trip as wrong type.
Name claims empty_array but body passes empty dict {}; a regression handling list input would not fail this test. Rename and add real array case.
Typo 'inalid' means -k invalid filtering misses this test, allowing invalid-payload regression to pass silently in filtered runs. Fix spelling.

issues.descricao: AssignmentSource.queued defaults to timezone.now() evaluated at class definition, so all instances share the import-time timestamp instead of the time they were queued.
issues.textoGolden: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates once at class-definition time so every AssignmentSource without explicit queued shares the same timestamp. WHY: queued time is wrong/stale for all later instances and defeats its purpose as a queue-time marker. HOW: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (with `field` import).

Field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import so all AssignmentSources share the same timestamp. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance measures its actual creation/queue time.

The dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value (which is exactly what `from_integration` does, and what `from_dict` falls back to when the key is absent) shares the same frozen import-time timestamp instead of the moment the assignment was actually queued. This makes the `queued` timestamp semantically wrong/meaningless (it reflects process start, not assignment time) and would silently misreport the queue time anywhere this value is later inspected. Fix by defaulting in a factory/`__post_init__` or making the caller pass the timestamp, e.g. set `queued` inside `from_integration` (`queued=timezone.now()`), or use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

issues.descricao: The test method name test_from_dict_inalid_data has a typo; it should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
issues.textoGolden: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.

comentarios.texto: Typo in test name test_from_dict_inalid_data hides it from name-filtered runs (e.g. -k invalid_data): fix spelling to test_from_dict_invalid_data so the invalid-payload guard is actually selected and verified.
