issues.descricao: The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
issues.textoGolden: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

comentarios.texto: The new occurrence builder accepts `value` but never incorporates or asserts it, so the occurrence tests cannot detect incorrect forwarding of the measured value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` supplies 10 for group_2 but builds its expected occurrence with 6 and still passes. A regression that passes a constant or another group's measurement at the new production hook would therefore go unnoticed. Include the value in the mock occurrence's evidence and use the actual expected measurement, or assert the hook's arguments directly.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it (the occurrence is built only from `group_key`/`new_status`), and this same helper is also the implementation of `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because neither the expected occurrence nor the handler output depends on the value, tests like `test_state_results_multi_group` (which incorrectly builds the group_2 occurrence with `value=6` while the packet carries `10`) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (expected built with 6 vs packet 8) pass regardless of the value actually passed into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If evaluation passed a wrong value, these tests would still pass, so they do not verify the value/threshold path they appear to cover. Include `value` in a field of the occurrence (or assert on it in the handler) and fix the wrong expected values so the argument is actually checked.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value: int` parameter but never uses it — the returned IssueOccurrence is derived only from `group_key` and `new_status`. Because `value` is dead, callers can pass a mismatched value with no failure: in `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet contains `group_2: 10`, but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `6`. Either use `value` when constructing the occurrence so the test validates the group value, or drop the unused parameter and pass the correct value; otherwise the test silently accepts wrong group values.

sugestoes.texto: Dead computation: `config` is copied and `schedule_type` is converted to display value, but the return dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (untransformed) instead of `config`, so the transformation never takes effect.

issues.descricao: get_failure_reason's docstring examples do not match the strings the function returns.

comentarios.texto: The `get_failure_reason` docstring describes output this function does not produce. The singular branch (line 146) returns a `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` value such as "A missed check-in was detected", yet the docstring advertises "A failed check-in was detected"; the multi-check-in branch joins `"%(count)d %(status)s"` fragments with `get_text_list(..., last_word=_("and"))` and appends " check-ins detected", yielding "2 missed and 1 error check-ins detected", not the docstring's "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". Update the examples (or the format string) so the documented contract matches the code.

The get_failure_reason docstring examples don't match the output. It shows 'A failed check-in was detected' and '...were detected', but the code returns the per-status singular strings ('A missed check-in was detected') or '<list> check-ins detected'. Update the examples to the real output and fix the 'humam readible' typo.

issues.descricao: get_monitor_environment_context builds a config copy with the human-readable schedule_type but returns the original monitor.config, so the conversion is lost and the context shows the raw value.
issues.textoGolden: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config to `config` and converts schedule_type display, but returns the original monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of `config`. WHY: the display conversion never takes effect so the occurrence context carries the raw schedule_type value, producing wrong output vs the function's evident intent. HOW: return `"config": config` instead of `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

Dead computation: `config` is copied and `config['schedule_type']` transformed to display value, but return uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (original) instead of `config`. Change to `"config": config` so transformation is used.

WHAT: In get_monitor_environment_context the code copies config and replaces config['schedule_type'] with the human-readable get_schedule_type_display(), but the returned context dict uses the original `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified local `config`, so the mutation is dead. WHY: The occurrence's monitor context always reports the raw schedule_type value rather than the display string the code intended to substitute, producing incorrect evidence data in the emitted occurrence. HOW: return the local variable, i.e. use "config": config in the returned dict.

issues.descricao: The newly added incidents.py and incident_occurrence.py define module loggers that are never used.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Line 114 compares two Dayjs objects with === which is always false, so zero-length (unavailable-day) date overrides are never detected. WHY: The find callback falls through, dateOverrideExist stays true and the function returns true, marking slots on fully-blocked override days as available. HOW: Replace reference equality with value comparison, e.g. dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,'minutes')).

WHAT: Working-hours check computes both start and end from slotStartTime, ignoring eventLength/slotEndTime. WHY: Slots whose end overflows workingHour.endTime are wrongly treated as inside working hours and returned as bookable past closing time. HOW: Compute end from slotEndTime, e.g. const end = slotEndTime.hour()*60+slotEndTime.minute().
end is computed identically to start from slotStartTime, so computed slotEndTime is never used and overlong slots spilling past workingHour.endTime pass. Derive end from slotEndTime.
=== compares object identity, two fresh Dayjs instances are never ===, so this branch cannot execute. Use .isSame() for value comparison.
When slot falls inside a date override the function returns true immediately, skipping the busy.every check below, so bookings on override days appear available. Fall through to busy check instead.
find only returns true when a same-day entry exists and slot is outside it; if no entry covers slotStartTime.day() find is falsy and slot proceeds as available. Must require a covering entry.

Execution break: override.timeZone is optional and invitee timeZone is unvalidated user input, but both are passed directly to dayjs().tz() which throws RangeError on undefined/unknown zone. Previously getUTCHours() never threw. Validate zones and wrap tz()/utcOffset() in try/catch with UTC fallback so one bad override cannot crash getSlots/getSchedule.

Execution break: truthy check guards undefined but not an invalid/unknown organizerTimeZone string; dayjs.tz() throws on invalid zone inside dateOverrides.find(), aborting checkIfIsAvailable/getSchedule. Validate against known zones or try/catch with fallback to 0.

Upper-bound of slot range reuses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so a slot starting inside workingHours but ending after workingHour.endTime is treated as available. Derive end from slotEndTime (slot start + eventLength).

checkIfIsAvailable interprets every dateOverride with global organizerTimeZone while producer attaches per-override timeZone and lib/slots.ts consumes it per-override; use date.timeZone fallback to organizerTimeZone so both sides agree.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that start within working hours but end after them are accepted.
issues.textoGolden: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — an exact duplicate of `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. WHY: the working-hours upper-bound test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore compares the slot START against the working-day end, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) overruns `workingHour.endTime` is never filtered and is reported as available, allowing bookings outside the host's working hours. HOW: compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();`.

`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so it always equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check is identical to the `start` check and never catches a slot that starts within working hours but ends past them. Use `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` for `end`.

`end` is computed identically to `start` (both from slotStartTime), so the check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` can never reject a slot on the upper bound. A slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is wrongly considered available; derive `end` from slotEndTime instead.

issues.descricao: The date-override check compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so zero-length (day off) overrides are never detected.
issues.textoGolden: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

comentarios.texto: This compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with `===` (reference equality), which is always false, so a zero-length override (start equal to end, whole day blocked) never returns true here. Compare timestamps, e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))`.

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate dayjs object references, so `===` is always false. The zero-length date-override branch is dead code and such an override is never recognised as covering the day; compare values (e.g. .isSame() or .valueOf() === .valueOf()) instead.

The equality check compares two separately created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length/closed-day rejection is unreachable, and a slot beginning exactly at that instant can reach the dateOverrideExist success return. Compare timestamps or use isSame instead.

issues.descricao: When a date override exists for the day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times, so slots overlapping existing bookings are reported available.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: when `dateOverrideExist` is true the function returns `true` before running the `busy.every(...)` check at the end. WHY: on any day that has a matching date override, a slot inside the override is reported available without checking the host's existing bookings (`busy` is spread via `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`), so a fixed/loose host who already has a booking during the override window is still shown as free — enabling double-booking. HOW: do not return early here; fall through so the override branch only decides whether the slot is inside the override window, and let the existing `busy` evaluation decide availability (e.g. `if (dateOverrideExist) { /* within override, still check busy */ } else { /* fall through to busy */ }`).

The new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits the `busy` conflict check (and the workingHours check) for any slot that falls inside a date override window. Every caller of `checkIfIsAvailable` previously counted on it returning false for a slot that overlaps an existing booking; on days covered by a date override that guarantee is gone, so slots conflicting with the user's real bookings are now reported as available and can be double-booked. The override branch should let control fall through to the `busy.every(...)` check (returning true only for the availability-window part) instead of returning early.

A matching date override returns true before checking busy periods. Both fixed-host and loose-host callers pass calendar and booking conflicts in busy, so a host with an override is offered even when an existing booking overlaps the slot. Continue to the busy checks after validating the override instead of returning true.

issues.descricao: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for the weekday excludes it, so split schedules (e.g. morning and afternoon) reject all slots.

comentarios.texto: The working-hours predicate rejects a slot if any interval on its weekday does not contain it. A split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 therefore loses every slot, since each valid slot lies outside the other interval. Require at least one matching interval to contain the full event instead of finding an interval that excludes it.

This search rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours window on that weekday. With split hours of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon window. Check for containment in at least one applicable window rather than finding any window that excludes the slot.

WHAT: Outside-working-hours test uses workingHours.find() returning true if ANY entry rejects the slot. WHY: With split schedules (two entries same weekday, e.g. morning+afternoon) a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon entry, find() matches and the slot is wrongly rejected as outside hours. HOW: Invert logic to accept if ANY entry contains the slot (e.g. !workingHours.some(entry contains slot) => outside).

issues.descricao: The date-override bound compares the slot start, not the slot end, with the override end, so slots extending past the override are accepted.

comentarios.texto: The override bounds reject only non-overlapping slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside an override. A fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability, despite being unavailable for its final half hour. Accept only when at least one override contains both slotStartTime and slotEndTime; this also avoids rejecting a slot merely because another interval on the same date does not overlap it.

The upper bound checks whether slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override end but finishes after it is treated as available. Compare slotEndTime with the override end using isAfter, so the slot must fit entirely inside the override.

issues.descricao: The override timezone conversion keeps only hour and minute, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone become inverted ranges or are applied to the wrong day.

comentarios.texto: Timezone conversion takes only hour and minute, discarding day rollover and turning intervals crossing attendee midnight into reversed ranges. A UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30, which buildSlots skips because start is greater than end, removing valid availability. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval across attendee-day boundaries before building slots.

WHAT: activeOverrides are filtered by UTC day (line 206-207) before the invitee/organizer offset is applied (lines 212-224), and shifted hours are not re-bucketed across midnight. WHY: An override that shifts to the previous/next calendar day in the invitee timezone is dropped from the wrong day or applied to the wrong day, so slots show open when the organizer is off (and vice versa). HOW: Filter/bucket overrides in the invitee-local date after applying the offset, or emit split entries spanning two invitee days.

issues.descricao: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

comentarios.texto: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

issues.descricao: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

The override day is computed with local-time dayjs(date.start) while the slot day is formatted in UTC, so on a server not running in UTC overrides near midnight are applied to the wrong day or skipped.
With several date-override ranges on the same day, a slot is rejected as soon as it falls outside any one of them, so slots inside the other ranges become unavailable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getCalendarCredentials calls async getCalendar without await, storing a Promise in the calendar field while remaining a sync function. WHY: Any caller other than the patched getConnectedCalendars that uses calendar.listCalendars/createEvent directly gets a Promise object, causing runtime TypeError and broken calendar listing/booking. HOW: Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar (Promise.all) and update all callers to await it.

WHAT: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) never awaits the async callbacks so calendar.deleteEvent promises are fire-and-forget. WHY: Reschedule proceeds to send emails without deleting old calendar/video events, leaving stale events and unhandled rejections that the surrounding code never catches. HOW: Replace forEach with await Promise.all(...map(async ...)) or for...of with await.

WHAT: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not await deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises and try/catch around forEach cannot catch async errors. WHY: Old calendar/video events are not reliably deleted on reschedule and failures become unhandled rejections instead of logged errors. HOW: Use await Promise.all with map or for...of with await inside the try block.

WHAT: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not await deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises and try/catch cannot catch async errors. WHY: Old calendar/video events are not reliably deleted on reschedule and failures become unhandled rejections. HOW: Use await Promise.all with map or for...of with await inside the try block.

WHAT: Recurring-event cancellation uses .forEach(async ...) that pushes into apiDeletes asynchronously after the outer flow already proceeds to await apiDeletes. WHY: Recurring calendar deleteEvent calls are skipped/late, leaving orphan events on provider calendars. HOW: Replace forEach with for...of with await or collect promises via map + Promise.all before pushing to apiDeletes.
forEach with async callback discards promises: outer try/catch cannot catch failures and reschedule does not wait for deleteEvent. Use await Promise.all with map or for...of with await.
forEach with async callback discards promises: outer try/catch cannot catch failures and reschedule does not wait for deleteEvent. Use await Promise.all with map or for...of with await.
forEach with async callback is not awaited, so deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are lost and errors become unhandled rejections. Use await Promise.all with map or for...of with await.

getCalendar() is now async (Promise<Calendar|null>) but getCalendarCredentials still calls it without await, so calendar field is a Promise, not a Calendar. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar (and await it at callers).

issues.descricao: Async callbacks passed to forEach after getCalendar became async are never awaited, so calendar and video cancellations run fire-and-forget, may not finish, and their errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections.
issues.textoGolden: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

comentarios.texto: The async forEach callback moves calendar factory exceptions outside the surrounding try/catch because forEach discards its returned promise. An invalid encrypted Exchange credential throws during CalendarService construction, now producing an unhandled rejection while Reschedule continues and returns success instead of logging the error; the identical regression occurs in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, so factory and deletion failures reach the catch.

The new async forEach callback is not awaited. If getCalendar rejects (for example, the dynamically imported calendar module fails to load or its service constructor throws), the callback produces a rejected promise that forEach discards; the surrounding try/catch cannot catch it. Previously a synchronous getCalendar failure reached that catch. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use an awaited for...of loop so these failures remain handled and calendar cleanup completes before rescheduling continues. Apply the same fix to the equivalent changed loop in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

WHAT: credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar; apiDeletes.push(...) }) pushes to apiDeletes asynchronously after outer code consumes it. WHY: outer apiDeletes is awaited elsewhere while async callbacks have not yet pushed, so recurring-event deletions are lost/partial and errors are unobserved. HOW: replace with for...of with await or collect promises via map + await Promise.all.

issues.descricao: Each import(...) in the appStore object literal runs when app-store/index.ts is imported, so all integrations still load at startup instead of lazily, while every entry becomes a promise.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid scheduled send then returns without deleting or updating the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: leaves stale scheduled WorkflowReminder rows for rescheduled/deleted workflows/steps that are never cleaned (cancelled flag never set), causing DB orphans and reprocessing. HOW: delete (or mark cancelled) the reminder row after the SendGrid cancel, mirroring the SMS path.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel loop queues Prisma deletes but a mid-loop throw skips Promise.all so queued deletes are never executed, and the catch only logs then continues scheduling. WHY: partially cancelled batch leaves cancelled reminders in DB while SendGrid state is unknown, so cancelled emails can still send or be retried inconsistently. HOW: await each delete inside the loop or collect promises with allSettled, and return/skip scheduling on failure.

WHAT: remindersToCancel is loaded unbounded and each SendGrid cancel is awaited sequentially inside the for loop. WHY: a large backlog of cancelled reminders blocks the cron with N serial network round-trips and unbounded memory, delaying all email scheduling. HOW: paginate/limit the findMany and issue SendGrid cancels concurrently with a bounded pool.
The verification-code TextField placeholder "Verification code" and Verify Button label are hard-coded English while neighbours use t() — route through translation function.

The immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row, unlike the SMS manager which always deletes. For kept bookings (reschedule path) this orphans the email reminder so it is never cleaned by the cancelled-reminder sweeper. Delete the row after successful cancel.

issues.descricao: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.textoGolden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.descricao: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

comentarios.texto: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

comentarios.texto: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

comentarios.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.descricao: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

comentarios.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

issues.descricao: The cron route sets the API key only on @sendgrid/mail, so the new @sendgrid/client cancellation requests are unauthenticated and reminders for cancelled bookings stay scheduled.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} so no column is updated. WHY: Prisma rejects empty update data and the comment intent to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never happens, breaking cache-status freshness and potentially throwing on every availability refresh. HOW: pass an explicit touch value e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

WHAT: handler directly instantiates CalendarCacheRepository instead of the calendar-cache.ts factory that returns CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when disabled. WHY: when calendar-cache is disabled it still issues prisma.calendarCache.groupBy and can expose status inconsistent with the rest of the app. HOW: resolve the repository through the existing factory that respects isCalendarCacheEnabledGlobally.

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation has no query invalidation while disconnectMutation invalidates connectedCalendars/integrations. WHY: after deleting cache the stale cacheUpdatedAt timestamp remains displayed until a manual refetch, making the new status UI incorrect. HOW: add onSettled invalidation of utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars like the disconnect path.

WHAT: sed -i '' -E uses BSD/macOS in-place syntax. WHY: on GNU/Linux sed interprets '' as a file operand and the webhook URL update fails, breaking the script on the primary dev/CI platform. HOW: use a portable in-place form e.g. sed -i.bak plus cleanup or branch on uname.

WHAT: fixed /tmp/tmole.log combined with rm -f and shell redirect follows symlinks. WHY: a local attacker pre-creating /tmp/tmole.log as a symlink causes truncation/overwrite of an arbitrary victim-owned file when the script runs. HOW: create the log with mktemp and avoid predictable paths.

Passing {} to updateManyByCredentialId forwards empty data to prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany which rejects empty data, so updatedAt is never bumped and the call can throw. Pass an explicit timestamp to satisfy the callee's Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput contract.
The comment declares an updatedAt bump but data is {} so Prisma updates no columns and @updatedAt does not fire. Pass an explicit timestamp so the write matches the declaration.

updateMany with empty data ({}) throws PrismaClientValidationError at runtime, so this line breaks the availability flow instead of bumping updatedAt. Pass an explicit field (e.g. updatedAt) or skip the call when there is nothing to update.

Date formatting is hard-coded to en-US while all surrounding user content goes through t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time for cache_last_updated. Use the locale from useLocale()/i18n instead of "en-US".

issues.descricao: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object, so Prisma does not refresh the @updatedAt timestamp and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never reflects the cache refresh.
issues.textoGolden: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany rejects empty data (validation error) or no-ops without touching @updatedAt, so the refresh path throws or silently leaves updatedAt stale. HOW: pass an explicit touch field e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

Comment claims "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt" but call passes empty object {} as data, so nothing is updated (Prisma updateMany with empty data is a no-op/error). Fix comment or pass { updatedAt: new Date() } to match the stated intent.

updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {}. Prisma updateMany throws when data is empty, so this line throws on every resync after the cache write. Pass an explicit touch e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() } instead of {}.

issues.descricao: After deleting the calendar cache, CredentialActionsDropdown does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so where no parent refetch callback is passed the stale cache status and delete action remain visible.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query, while the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`. WHY: the 'Cache Status' row in the dropdown is rendered from the cached `connectedCalendars` result; after deleting the cache the query is not refetched, so the deleted status/last-updated entry stays visible and stale in the UI. HOW: invalidate the query in the cache-deletion mutation as well, e.g. `const utils = trpc.useUtils(); onSuccess: async () => { ...; await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }`.

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only calls onSuccess?.() and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation onSettled. WHY: cacheUpdatedAt stays stale after deletion so UI keeps showing old Last updated and delete action until manual refetch. HOW: add onSettled invalidate of connectedCalendars like disconnect does.

Successful cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion.

issues.descricao: The cache 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale instead of the user's locale, so non-US users see US-style dates in an otherwise translated label.
issues.textoGolden: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

comentarios.texto: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale (new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)), so every user — regardless of their locale — sees a US-style date/time while the surrounding label is translated. Use the app's locale-aware date formatting helper (the user's current locale) instead of pinning en-US.

Date format hard-coded to "en-US" via Intl.DateTimeFormat while surrounding strings use t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time. Use the active locale from useLocale/i18n instead of hard-coding "en-US".

The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

issues.descricao: The calendar cache migration keeps a generated warning saying updatedAt has no default and cannot be added to a non-empty table, although the SQL adds it with DEFAULT NOW().

comentarios.texto: This warning says updatedAt is added without a default and cannot be added to a nonempty table, but the migration actually supplies DEFAULT NOW(), explicitly handling existing rows. Remove or correct the warning so operators reviewing the migration are not incorrectly told that existing data makes it unsafe to run.

issues.descricao: The test-gcal-webhooks.sh cleanup function always exits 0, including when called from the failure paths, so the script reports success when the tunnel could not be set up.

comentarios.texto: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also called on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed to extract the URL). The script therefore reports success even though the tunnel failed and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated. Have `cleanup` take an exit code, and pass 1 from the failure paths.

cleanup() always ends in `exit 0`, and both failure paths (rate-limit at lines 46-50 and 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' at lines 56-59) call cleanup. So a script named test-gcal-webhooks that did not actually obtain the tunnel URL / update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL still exits with status 0, letting any automation treat the run as successful even though the setup it verifies failed. On the failure branches the script should exit non-zero (e.g. `exit 1`) so failure is observable; only the SIGINT/SIGTERM interactive shutdown should exit 0.

issues.descricao: The webhook test script updates .env with the macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on Linux GNU sed and leaves GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged.
issues.textoGolden: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|' "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` form. WHY: under GNU sed (typical Linux dev/CI environment) the empty `''` is consumed as the script operand and the command errors, so the existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line is never replaced and the tunnel URL is not written to the env file. HOW: use a portable invocation, e.g. `sed -i.bak -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` (or branch on `uname`).

The environment update uses BSD sed's `-i ''` syntax, which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it was updated, preventing webhooks from reaching the new tunnel. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the in-place syntax based on the available sed implementation and check its exit status.

When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, `sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. The script nevertheless prints that the URL was updated and keeps the tunnel running, leaving webhooks configured with the old URL. Use a portable replacement approach (or select the appropriate sed syntax) and only announce success after the edit succeeds.

issues.descricao: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the user, so tRPC returns a 500 instead of a structured FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error.
issues.textoGolden: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up with exact case-sensitive `where(email: email)` on the raw value. WHY: An attacker blocked as `bad@spam.com` can sign up as `BAD@spam.com` (or with case/whitespace variants) because email identity is case-insensitive, defeating the block. HOW: Normalize with `Email.downcase(email.to_s.strip)` on write and lookup, or query case-insensitively.

WHAT: should_block? does read-modify-write `match_count += 1` followed by `save`. WHY: Concurrent blocked signups read the same count and overwrite each other, losing increments and making last_match_at ordering unreliable. HOW: Use atomic `increment_counter`/`update_counters` for match_count plus a separate timestamp update.

WHAT: emailValidation depends on `rejectedEmails.@each` while the array holds primitive strings pushed via `pushObject`. WHY: `@each` observes properties of array items, not membership, so pushing a blocked email does not invalidate the computed property and the error is not shown until the email field itself changes. HOW: Depend on `rejectedEmails.[]` (or `rejectedEmails.length) instead of `rejectedEmails.@each`.

WHAT: validate_each calls should_block?, which does a SELECT plus a synchronous UPDATE (`match_count`/`last_match_at` save) inside the validation path. WHY: Every User validation with a changed email pays an extra read and, on match, a write; repeated valid? calls inflate match_count and slow the signup hot path with avoidable writes. HOW: Split into a side-effect-free check for validation and update stats once when the signup actually fails.

Case-sensitivity bypass: should_block? uses exact-case where(email: email) while sibling checks are case-insensitive. Blocked bad@spam.com can be bypassed with BAD@Spam.COM. Normalize both sides before comparing email identity.

Read-modify-write (match_count+=1 + save) races: two concurrent should_block? calls read the same count and both write count+1, losing an increment and racing last_match_at. Use an atomic DB increment (update_all/increment_counter) instead of in-memory += and save.

Comment claims last_match_at indicates 'have ever been blocked', but BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match_count/last_match_at for every match including action_type :do_nothing (proven by shared examples for both :block and :do_nothing). A do_nothing hit sets last_match_at without blocking, so the prose is untrue. Fix the comment to say matched/seen, not blocked.

Name should_block? promises a pure predicate but the body writes to the DB (match_count increment, last_match_at update, save) on every call, even for :do_nothing. Callers reading the name expect no mutation. Rename to reflect the recording side effect or split query from recording.

issues.descricao: When the server rejects an email, the signup form marks it with the generic 'invalid email' text instead of the server's reason (blocked or not allowed).

comentarios.texto: The message shown for a rejected email disagrees with the reason the code is reacting to. This branch fires when the server rejected the email (result.errors.email), and this PR gives that condition its own server string — user.email.blocked, added in config/locales/server.en.yml as "is not allowed." — but the client re-labels it with the generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). A user whose address is perfectly well-formed but blocked/hosted on a blacklisted domain is therefore told their email is invalid, contradicting the reason just returned by the server. Use the blocked/not-allowed message (and add a matching client locale key) instead of user.email.invalid. Notice the same generic string is used at line ~94 for validation failures, so it should not be reused to represent a distinct server-side rejection.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email with a case-sensitive exact match and no normalisation, so changing the letter case of a blocked address bypasses the block list.
issues.textoGolden: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

comentarios.texto: Blocked-email lookup compares the raw email without normalizing its domain. A signup for block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG does not match a blocked record for block@spamfromhome.org despite identifying the same mailbox, allowing the signup restriction to be bypassed by changing domain capitalization. Normalize domains using Email.downcase both when storing blocked emails and when looking them up.

Canonicalize blocked emails consistently with the application's Email.downcase identity handling, both when storing entries and when looking them up. This exact equality query is case-sensitive, and BlockedEmail's validation callback only defaults action_type. A block-list entry such as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` therefore does not block the same identity submitted/stored as `block@spamfromhome.org`. This is particularly relevant to the explicitly supported manually populated block list. Normalize existing/imported entries as well as new ones, and add a test with differing casing between the stored entry and the lookup.
Case-sensitivity bypass: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is exact case-sensitive with no normalization, while sibling checks are case-insensitive. Normalize (downcase/strip) on write and lookup.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match_count and last_match_at as a side effect of email validation, so each signup attempt (validated twice) inflates the counter and concurrent updates can lose increments.
issues.textoGolden: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: should_block? mutates match_count/last_match_at via read-modify-write save inside a validator. WHY: Every validation call (including re-validations of the same attempt or attempts failing on unrelated fields like username) inflates stats, and concurrent signups lose increments with no atomic update. HOW: Move stats update out of validation or use atomic increment (update_counters/increment_counter) only on actual blocked rejections.

WHAT: `should_block?` mutates state (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, calls `record.save`) inside a method that is invoked from the model validation callback, and the signup controller runs validation twice per attempt (`user.valid?` at users_controller.rb:168 then `user.save` at :172). WHY: a single signup attempt increments `match_count` twice and rewrites `last_match_at`, so the per-email block statistics the feature was built to track are wrong. HOW: make the read side non-mutating for validation and record the match separately (e.g. move the increment out of validation, or guard it so it runs once per attempt), keeping the predicate pure.

WHAT: `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no lock or unique constraint protection. WHY: two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` and one write overwrites the other, losing counts, so the tracked statistics drift under load. HOW: use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or a database-level counter increment.

issues.descricao: Claims the 'returns false' spec cannot distinguish nil from false because be_false is a truthiness matcher.

comentarios.texto: This test is named "returns false if a record with the email doesn't exist," but it cannot verify that. `BlockedEmail.should_block?` returns `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]`, which yields `nil` (not `false`) when no record exists, and under this suite's RSpec 2 semantics `subject.should be_false` is a truthiness matcher that passes for any falsy value including `nil`. The assertion therefore passes on the nil the code actually returns and would only fail on an outright `true`; it does not pin the `false`/`nil` distinction its name asserts. Assert the value exactly (e.g. `subject.should == false`, or `be_falsey`/`be_nil` if nil is intended) so a regression returning a non-false falsy value is caught.

issues.descricao: The domain whitelist/blacklist regex @(domains) is not anchored at the end, so an address like user@example.com.evil.com matches a whitelist entry for example.com and bypasses the restriction.
issues.textoGolden: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: email_in_restriction_setting? builds unanchored Regexp "@(domains)" with only '.' escaped. WHY: Whitelist 'gmail.com' substring-matches 'victim@gmail.com.evil.com', so an attacker registers with an unapproved domain and bypasses the allow-list; blacklist similarly over/under-matches and other regex metachars are unescaped. HOW: Anchor and escape domains (e.g. Regexp.escape per domain split on '|' plus /\A[^@\s]+@(?:domain)\z/i).

issues.descricao: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when the user has no row, then tu.notification_level dereferences nil. WHY: Crashes the new GET unsubscribe endpoint with NoMethodError (500) for the common regular/default state instead of unsubscribing. HOW: Handle nil (e.g. TopicUser.get/change with default) and nil notification_level (COALESCE to regular) before comparing/saving.

WHAT: Per-topic unsubscribe mutates notification_level via GET (t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe -> topics#unsubscribe with tu.save!). WHY: GET is exempt from CSRF protection, so an attacker can force a logged-in victim's browser (img tag, prefetch, crawler) to mute/downgrade topics without consent. HOW: Make the mutation POST/PUT/DELETE with CSRF token and keep GET as confirmation page only.

WHAT: unsubscribe_link now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} but MessageBuilder does not guarantee it is present when add_unsubscribe_link is true. WHY: Any email built with add_unsubscribe_link:true without unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fails to send. HOW: Default unsubscribe_url to user_preferences_url or guard interpolation in MessageBuilder html_part/body.
TopicUser.find_by returns nil when no row exists, so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and request 500s. Ensure record exists before dereferencing.

The PR adds unsubscribe_url to the fixture but no assertion checks it. Both tests (List-Unsubscribe header present, user_preferences_url in body) pass even if unsubscribe_url is dropped or not rendered, so breakage of the new per-topic unsubscribe link is undetected. Add an assertion that the body/header contains the supplied unsubscribe_url.

TopicUser.find_by can return nil (row created lazily) and notification_level can be nil, so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link 500s. Guard the nil cases before comparing levels.

Topic#unsubscribe_url returns a site-relative path, but user_notifications.rb passes it as unsubscribe_url into emails where server.en.yml renders it as [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}). Email clients need an absolute URL (compare user_preferences_url which includes Discourse.base_url). Prefix with Discourse.base_url or build the absolute URL at the mailer call site.

Triple-brace {{{...}}} disables escaping for a string built from I18n topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications interpolated with model.fancyTitle. Neighbouring line uses {{i18n ...}} (escaped). If the title contains HTML, it is injected into the page. Use double braces or escape the title before interpolation.

Identifier stopNotificiationsText misspells 'Notifications' (extra 'i'), disagreeing with locale key stop_notifications and user-visible prose. Rename to stopNotificationsText in controller and template so the name matches the documented intent.

unsubscribe_link gained required %{unsubscribe_url} but Email::MessageBuilder just forwards template_args to I18n.t without a default, so any existing add_unsubscribe_link:true caller that does not pass unsubscribe_url now raises MissingInterpolation (spec itself had to be fixed). Provide a fallback or keep old template working when unsubscribe_url is absent.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

issues.descricao: The message builder spec passes unsubscribe_url in the fixture but never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the email.

comentarios.texto: The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

issues.descricao: The unsubscribe confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, which still sends mention/reply notifications.

comentarios.texto: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

issues.descricao: Unsubscribe saves the new notification level without setting notifications_reason_id, so auto-tracked topics are promoted back to tracking on the next read, undoing the unsubscribe.

comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

issues.descricao: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText).
issues.textoGolden: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

issues.descricao: The topic unsubscribe GET endpoint is not idempotent: each visit steps the notification level down again, so reloading the link moves a topic from regular to muted.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Light-theme branch uses $lightness 70% while the original was $lightness 30%. WHY: Light-theme users see a much lighter/washed-out author link, a visual regression vs pre-PR. HOW: Restore first arg to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with secondary complement 70%.

WHAT: Light-theme branch uses $lightness 30% while the original was $lightness 70%. WHY: Light-theme hint text becomes much darker than intended, breaking the de-emphasized hint style. HOW: Restore first arg to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) with secondary complement 30%.

WHAT: Light-theme branch uses $lightness 50% while the original was $lightness 20%. WHY: Light-theme topic-map heading renders lighter than designed, reducing hierarchy/contrast. HOW: Restore first arg to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) with secondary complement 80%.

WHAT: Light-theme branch uses $lightness 50% while the original was $lightness 30% for .group-member-info .name. WHY: Light-theme username renders lighter than before, inconsistent with adjacent elements and original design. HOW: Restore first arg to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with secondary complement 70%.

WHAT: Light-theme branch uses $lightness 50% while the original was $lightness 30% for .name. WHY: Same light-theme regression as desktop — username appears lighter than intended. HOW: Restore first arg to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with secondary complement 70%.

Original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but replacement uses 70% as first arg of dark-light-choose, changing light-theme output. Every other 30% conversion in this PR preserves 30%/70%. Fix first arg back to 30% / second to 70%.
Same selector .custom-message-length in desktop/modal.scss converts 70% to 70%/30% but mobile converts 70% to 30%/70%. The two sites must agree; mobile first arg should be 70% lightness, second 30%.

Original h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and desktop/topic-post.scss correctly converts to 20%/80%, but mobile converts to 50%/50%. Light-theme value changes and desktop/mobile disagree. Restore 20%/80%.

Original .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but replacement uses 50%/50%, changing light-theme output. The matching .name in common/base/user.scss correctly uses 30%/70%. Fix to 30%/70%.

issues.descricao: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the light-theme color changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 70% because the dark-light-choose arguments were inverted, making the link much paler in light themes.
issues.textoGolden: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

comentarios.texto: The light-theme argument was changed from the original lightness. WHAT: the original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new value uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the first (light-theme) argument is now 70%, not 30%. WHY: this silently darkens the light-theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` (post-author link) from a 30% to a 70% tint, a light-theme regression outside the PR's dark-theme-only intent; the values also are inverted relative to the (X, 100−X) convention used everywhere else (should be 30/70). HOW: use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

The original value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). After conversion the light-mode argument became $primary:70% and dark-mode $secondary:30% — both inverted away from the original 30%. Should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). As written the light-mode color is dramatically lighter than intended.

This bold link inside `.reply`/`nav.post-controls` was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The rewrite uses 70% as the light-theme argument, inverting the intended value (the complementary pair should be 30/70, not 70/30). The light theme now shows this link far lighter than before; the first argument must remain the original 30%.

issues.textoGolden: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

comentarios.texto: The light-theme argument was changed from the original lightness. WHAT: the original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the first argument is now 30%, not 70%. WHY: this changes the light-theme color of `.custom-message-length` from a 70% to a 30% tint (a light-theme regression), and the pair is inverted vs. the (X, 100−X) convention; the desktop counterpart at desktop/modal.scss:94 correctly kept 70/30. HOW: use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

The original `.custom-message-length` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The refactor changed the light-theme argument to 30%, so the light theme now renders this hint much darker than before (a 40-point lightness jump). It also no longer matches its desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss keeps `70%, 30%`). The first argument must stay at the original 70%: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

`.custom-message-length` now contradicts the desktop rule for the same class. desktop/modal.scss (line 94) converted the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` (keeping 70%), while this hunk produced `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, flipping the primary lightness 70→30. Both files started from 70%, so mobile should be 70/30 to agree with desktop and preserve the original value.

issues.textoGolden: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).

comentarios.texto: The `.name` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `50%` in the light branch. This changes the light-theme color. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

The .name color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but the light argument was changed to 50%, so the light theme loses its contrast. Use dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

The .name light value was changed from primary 30% to 50%, which lightens the text in light mode. Use dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

issues.textoGolden: In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

WHAT: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` (30% → 50%). The light-theme value no longer matches the original. WHAT: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and now is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` (20% → 50%). WHY: this visibly lightens the topic-map heading in the light theme; the desktop counterpart at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 correctly kept 20% (20/80), so mobile diverged. HOW: use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

Original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The conversion changed it to 50%/50%, but the desktop mirror of this rule (desktop/topic-post.scss h3) uses 20%/80%. The two files must agree; should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)).

This `h3` was originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The rewrite changed the light-theme argument to 50%, so the light theme renders the heading lighter than before; the correct pair is 20/80, not 50/50. The first argument must keep the original 20%.

issues.descricao: The comment describing the topic-list cell default color still names a plain scale-color($primary, 50%) rule that the PR replaced with dark-light-choose.

comentarios.texto: The comment at lines 72-74 states "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)", but the rule it documents was converted by this PR to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-X%))` (here for coldmap-high/med/low and in common/base/_topic-list.scss th/td). The prose still names a single `$primary` expression, so it no longer describes the code: a reader comparing the two will look for a plain `$primary` 50% rule that no longer exists. Update the comment to describe the dark-light-choose baseline (e.g. "is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))").

issues.descricao: In dark themes the notification badge background becomes a lightened $secondary while its text stays $secondary, giving dark text on a dark background with poor contrast.

comentarios.texto: The dark-theme notification badge background now uses a lightened $secondary while its text still uses the unmodified $secondary. This puts dark text on a dark background for plain badges such as category unread counts in site-map.hbs:73; with $secondary black, the foreground is #000 and the background is approximately #4d4d4d (about 2.5:1 contrast), making the small count text difficult to read. Set the default badge foreground, including its &[href] rule, to a contrasting dark-theme color such as $primary when selecting this dark background.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The conditional is named include_website_name without the trailing ? required by ActiveModel::Serializer 0.8. WHY: The guard is never called so website_name is always serialized, breaking the intended website.present? contract. HOW: Rename to include_website_name? to match every other predicate in the same file (include_email?, include_stats?, etc.).

WHAT: URI without a scheme has nil host, so website_name returns nil even when website is present. WHY: The template gates on {{#if model.website_name}}, so a stored value like example.com/user disappears instead of showing fallback host text. HOW: Normalize by prepending a scheme before parsing when host is nil, or fall back to the raw website value.

WHAT: Same-domain display concatenates only host + path, discarding query and fragment. WHY: A website like http://example.com/user?ref=x displays as example.com/user, losing distinguishing information and mismatching the href. HOW: Append query/fragment (e.g. use request_uri) when present.

AMS checks include_<attr>? with trailing ?. include_website_name without ? is never invoked, so website_name is always serialized even when website is blank. Rename to include_website_name? to match :website_name and sibling hooks like include_card_image_badge_id?

issues.descricao: website_name compares hostnames case-sensitively, so an uppercase website host matching the instance domain shows only the host instead of the full path.

comentarios.texto: The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Normalise both sides before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` (or use `URI(...).hostname`, which down-cases) and compare against `Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`.

Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. With an instance hostname of example.com and a valid website of http://EXAMPLE.COM/user, neither the exact-host nor suffix comparison matches, so the profile displays only EXAMPLE.COM instead of the requested path. Normalize both hostnames to lowercase for comparison while preserving the desired display spelling.

issues.descricao: website_name strips only the first label to decide same-domain, so unrelated hosts under multi-label public suffixes (co.uk, github.io) are treated as the instance domain and shown with full path.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `elsif` branch treats the last two dot-segments as the registrable domain, so multi-part public suffixes are mis-compared. WHY: for e.g. website_host='example.co.uk' and discourse_host='forum.co.uk' both have 3 segments, the branch compares `'co.uk' == 'co.uk'`, concludes the domains match, and returns `website_host + path`, even though example.co.uk and forum.co.uk are unrelated sites — the display then shows a path that does not belong to the instance domain, defeating the feature's purpose. HOW: compare against a public-suffix-aware registrable domain (e.g. use the PublicSuffix list) or require at least the full suffix before treating hosts as the same domain, instead of blindly taking `split('.')[1..-1]`.

Comparing all labels except the first incorrectly treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, with instance host `forum.co.uk` and website `https://unrelated.co.uk/user`, this returns `unrelated.co.uk/user` rather than the unrelated-site host-only label. Both hosts have three labels and their suffixes are `co.uk`, so this branch mistakes the public suffix for a shared site domain. Use registrable-domain-aware comparison (or a narrower explicit host relationship) before including the path.

The same-label-count branch treats two hosts as the same domain when everything after the first label matches. Unrelated hosts on shared suffixes, such as `a.github.io` and `b.github.io`, are treated as the same domain, so the full path is shown for an unrelated website. Compare against the registrable domain, for example with the PublicSuffix gem, or drop this heuristic branch.

issues.descricao: Claims website_name should also show the full path when the website is a subdomain of the instance host.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Else branch only tests `discourse_host.ends_with?('.'+website_host)` (discourse child of website) and misses the reverse (website subdomain of instance). WHY: With instance `example.com` and website `http://sub.example.com/page`, it returns `sub.example.com` instead of `sub.example.com/page`, contradicting the PR intent to show the full path for same-base-domain URLs. HOW: Also return host+path when `website_host` ends with `.`+discourse_host or shares the same registrable domain.

issues.descricao: website_name is not marked untrusted, so the host/path of a TL0 user's website, which is hidden from anonymous viewers, is still exposed through the new field.
